articles.title: After Hindu Raksha Dal claims attack, saffron-clad groups threaten protesters again
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Saffron-clad groups carrying sticks were seen threatening demonstrators in central Delhi for a second consecutive day on Sunday, a day after
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Saffron-clad groups carrying sticks were seen threatening demonstrators in central Delhi for a second consecutive day on Sunday, a day after the Hindu Raksha Dal claimed responsibility for an assault on protesters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The comments came after police arrested four men in connection with Saturday's alleged assault on DDU Marg.According to PTI, several men carrying sticks moved around Connaught Place, where demonstrations were taking place, confronting protesters and issuing threats. Their presence came despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) being in force.On Saturday, groups of men wearing saffron scarves and raising religious slogans were seen moving around protest sites, threatening demonstrators and openly defending violence against those protesting the Election Commission (EC). Some claimed they had turned up in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and were unconcerned about being detained by police.The men accused protesters of raising "anti-national and anti-Modi" slogans, with some describing them as "anti-national elements" who "deserved to be thrashed". Groups were also heard shouting, "Delhi Police tum lath bajao, hum tumhare saath hain (Delhi Police, you wield the baton, we are with you)".The incidents unfolded as thousands of protesters were detained across the capital during demonstrations demanding Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the EC's functioning and its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A widely circulated video purportedly showed two men assaulting a male protester and manhandling a woman, pushing her to the ground and pulling at her clothes. The footage also appeared to show police personnel at the scene. Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was among those who shared a screenshot of the alleged assault.Hindu Raksha Dal chief Pinki Chaudhary subsequently shared the video on X, claiming the attackers were members of his organisation. "These are my workers from the Hindu Raksha Dal, an organisation that delivers on its promises," he wrote, adding that the outfit could set the minds of "cockroaches" straight.In another post, Chaudhary described the men as "warriors" of Sanatan Dharma and warned, "We have no interest in politics, but if anyone targets Sanatan, we will target them and send them exactly where they belong." He tagged the Prime Minister's Office and the offices of the Uttar Pradesh and Delhi chief ministers.Police identified the four arrested men as Raman Saini, 50; Vivekanand alias Vivek, 32; Kapil Kumar, 27; and Ravinder Singh alias Govind Hindu, 35.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: The ABCD of US politics: American-born Combative Desis face MAGA heat
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The daughter of Indian immigrants is challenging one of New York’s most powerful Democrats.
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: The daughter of Indian immigrants is challenging one of New York’s most powerful Democrats. In Colorado, an Indian-American Republican is running for attorney general. And across the country, candidates of Indian origin are seeking office under both the Democratic and Republican banners, extending a political presence that is no longer confined to Congress.While much of the attention in the US midterm elections on November 3 is focused on congressional contests and gubernatorial races featuring candidates such as Democrat Ro Khanna in California (for the House of Representatives) and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio (for the Governor’s mansion), the growing desi footprint reaches further down the ballot -- to state attorneys general, legislatures and local government.One of the most striking examples is Saritha Komatireddy, the Republican challenging New York Attorney General Letitia James. Until recently, Komatireddy was hardly a household name outside legal and Republican political circles. But a combative televised debate with James on October 8 has given her greater visibility and a much larger platform.It’s an uphill battle: New York is heavily Democratic, James is an established political figure who prosecuted Donald Trump, and Komatireddy is making her first run for elected office. Yet the challenger has turned her legal credentials and tough-on-crime message into a campaign that is attracting attention well beyond her prospects of actually winning, including an editorial thumbs-up from the Wall Street Journal.Komatireddy, 41, was born in Brooklyn to parents who emigrated from India in the 1980s. A Harvard Law School graduate, she clerked for Brett Kavanaugh before his elevation to the Supreme Court, worked as a federal prosecutor in Brooklyn, and served as chief of staff at the Drug Enforcement Administration under President Biden. Her prosecutorial career included terrorism and narcotics cases, and she was nominated for a federal judgeship that failed to materialise.Komatireddy is not alone in seeking a statewide legal office. In Colorado, Hetal Doshi, a first-generation Indian-American and former federal prosecutor, entered the Democratic race for attorney general. She previously served as a deputy assistant attorney general in the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division. Her candidacy illustrates how Indian-American professionals are competing for offices that extend well beyond the familiar terrain of immigration and foreign policy.The congressional contests offer another measure of that growing reach. Four Indian-American Democrats in the outgoing House -- Ro Khanna and Ami Bera of California, Pramila Jayapal of Washington, and Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia -- are seeking re-election. Meanwhile, Democrat Amish Shah, a physician born to Gujarati immigrant parents, is running in Arizona’s 1st Congressional District, and Pia Dandiya, an educator and former school principal whose parents emigrated from India, is contesting Florida’s 22nd District. Both have received backing from the Democratic leadership.On the Republican side, Vivek Ramaswamy, the Cincinnati-born son of Indian immigrants, is running for governor with President Trump’s endorsement. His candidacy offers a reminder that Indian-American political identity does not dictate party allegiance: Ramaswamy’s conservative message and Komatireddy’s law-and-order campaign stand in sharp contrast to the progressive politics of Jayapal and Khanna.But the path to political acceptance is not always as straightforward as a Republican label might suggest. Some hard-line MAGA activists have made clear that conservative credentials do not necessarily trump race, ancestry or religion. Ramaswamy has faced attacks from within the right, including a primary rival who derided him as an “Indian boy” pretending to be American. Other critics have questioned how a Hindu can represent a state whose population is predominantly Christian.The backlash against Indian professionals during the MAGA movement’s bitter H-1B visa debate has reinforced the contradiction: Indian-Americans can be celebrated as successful entrepreneurs and political allies while being cast by nativists as outsiders competing for American jobs and cultural influence. Even Indian-American Republicans have faced hostility over their heritage or religion. For candidates such as Ramaswamy, the test is therefore not simply whether voters accept their politics, but whether the movement they represent will accept them as fully American.You use AI every day. articles.body: Egypt on Sunday presented a restored version of the “Tondo of the Two Brothers”, a celebrated painting dating to the second century and part of the renowned Fayoum portrait collection.The restoration took three weeks, with experts from Rome working alongside conservators at the Egyptian museum in Tahrir, where the collection is normally housed, officials said at a press conference.Fayoum mummy portraits were typically created on thin wooden panels and placed over the faces of the dead beneath their mummy wrappings. The artworks reflect a fusion of Egyptian burial traditions and artistic styles from the broader Greco-Roman world.Egypt is preparing to loan a substantial portion of the collection for a temporary exhibition in Rome. The upcoming display will mark the collection's first journey outside the country.Egyptian minister of tourism and antiquities Sherif Fathy said the restoration demonstrated how cooperation between countries could help safeguard and study cultural heritage.“The restoration of the Tondo of the Two Brothers is an important example of what can be achieved through international cooperation in the preservation and study of cultural heritage,” Fathy said.“Egypt and Italy share deep historical and cultural ties, and this project brings together Egyptian and Italian expertise to preserve an exceptional work of art for future generations,” he added.The painting stands out for its circular design and its portrayal of two figures, unlike the single-person subjects found in many other portraits. Experts consider it one of the most strikingly lifelike works to have survived from Roman-era Egypt.The artwork was made using a technique in which pigments are blended with molten wax. During the restoration, specialists managed to bring back the facial features of the brother positioned on the right, according to AP.Aly Abdel Halim, director general of the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir, said the conservation work required a delicate approach as the wooden panel had suffered termite damage and the painted surface was also fragile.The restored portraits will be displayed in Rome at an exhibition scheduled to run from November through May 2027.Tomaso Radaelli, chairman of MondoMostre, the exhibition's organiser, said the show would feature more than 110 artefacts. These will include painted panels, funerary shrouds, masks, marble portraits, plaster casts and ancient jewellery.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Zelenskyy hits back after Trump's remark, says ready to hold Ukraine elections if Russia offers 60-day ceasefire
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that he would organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to a 60-day
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that he would organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire, responding to criticism from US President Donald Trump over his leadership."Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organize elections," Zelenskyy told the ABC.Trump had criticised Zelenskyy on Saturday for targeting Russian oil refineries, a day after the United States temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were intended to deprive Moscow of revenue to fund its war in Ukraine."I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump told reporters at the White House.Responding to the remarks, Zelenskyy said the choice of Ukraine's leader rested with its people and noted that Putin would also like to see a change in the country's leadership.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine was being blamed for rising fuel prices even though the war in the Middle East was driving up prices globally.Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was prepared to stop attacking Russian oil refineries if Moscow halted its strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.Meanwhile, Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate ceasefire targeting energy infrastructure, urging both sides to adhere to the arrangement."Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Trump said in a post on Truth Social.However, Zelenskyy told news outlet Axios that he had not been aware of the energy ceasefire announcement made by Trump earlier on Sunday. He added that Ukraine would accept such an arrangement if Russia agreed to it."The ceasefire announcement was news for me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire, Ukraine will agree. If President Trump negotiated it with Putin. Please tell us when the ceasefire begins, we are ready and we will accept it," Zelenskyy said, as per Axios.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, California began filling a 750-acre expansion of the Salton Sea wetlands; the project aims to create wildlife habitat while reducing dust from the drying shoreline
articles.summary: In 2025, California took significant steps to restore the Salton Sea by flooding three square miles of exposed lakebed to create new wetland habitats while reducing harmful dust emissions. This project, part of the Species Conservation Habitat Project, aims to provide essential habitats for wildlife and improve air quality in surrounding communities.
articles.body: As the Salton Sea recedes, the exposed lakebed creates two major environmental concerns: habitat loss and dust that wind can carry into nearby communities. California reached a restoration milestone in 2025 when water began filling the East Pond Expansion, part of the state's Species Conservation Habitat (SCH) Project. The East Pond Expansion covers approximately 750 acres. Together with the existing East Pond, the two ponds account for a combined area of approximately 2,000 acres.The East Pond Expansion adds to California's restoration effortsThe filling of the East Pond Expansion was announced by the California Department of Water Resources on May 22, 2025. The department described the milestone as part of the state's effort to restore habitat and improve environmental conditions around the Salton Sea. It is estimated that the East Pond Expansion has an area of approximately 750 acres (or 1.2 square miles). Together with the East Pond, which has been filling since early April 2025, the total area of these two ponds to become operational in the coming weeks is 2,000 acres. The total area of 2,000 acres must not be mistaken for the area of the expansion. The SCH project will cover more than 9,000 acres (or 14 square miles) upon completion. The project includes shallow ponds, berms, nesting and loafing islands, and water delivery systems designed to sustain fish and bird populations. These features are important because the Salton Sea lies along the Pacific Flyway, a route used by migratory birds traveling between breeding and wintering grounds. As the lake recedes and its salinity rises, aquatic habitats and the food resources that support wildlife can change or disappear. The SCH Project is intended to restore some of this habitat while reducing dust from selected areas of exposed lakebed.Exposed playa threatens air quality in nearby communitiesPlaya is another threat in addition to habitat destruction. Winds can lift small particles from exposed soils, blowing the dust into nearby areas. Imperial Valley residents already struggle with air quality problems, and thus the control of dust in the region around the Salton Sea is a public health problem. The paper "Air Quality and Wheeze Symptoms in a Rural Children's Cohort Near a Drying Saline Lake," published in the journal Environmental Research, has investigated the link between respiratory symptoms and particulate matter exposure among 722 primarily Latino or Hispanic children. Caregivers provided information on the children's respiratory symptoms, whereas researchers used air-monitoring data to estimate dust-storm hours. The research defines a dust-storm hour as one when PM10 concentrations exceed 150 micrograms per cubic meter.The study did not find the same association among children living 11 kilometres or farther from the Salton Sea. Among children living less than 11 kilometres from the Salton Sea, every additional 100 hours of dust-storm exposure per year was associated with a 9.5-percentage-point increase in wheezing and a 4.6-percentage-point increase in bronchitic symptoms.It is possible to use water to prevent dust emission from exposed sediments. This technique does not prevent all air emissions from the sources; however, it helps reduce emissions from treated parts of the shoreline, which is gradually receding. The SCH project is aimed at restoring the habitat along with suppressing dust storms.Restored wetlands offer habitat for fish and migratory birdsThe SCH Project aims to deal with habitat losses in relation to the reduction of the surface area and increased salinity in the Salton Sea. Aquatic habitat can be created through shallow ponds, and nesting/loafing islands will serve as sites for resting and breeding for birds. Water quality is also crucial for the fish and other animals making up the food web. There is an additional 2024 study, Hydrogeologic and hydrochemical inputs to emerging wetlands on the shores of the receding Salton Sea, California, which studied the water sources and water quality at the Bombay Beach Wetlands. In particular, there were two proposed water sources: thermal artesian water or a combination of thermal artesian water and sediment water from the receding shoreline. Since the mentioned study does not consider the SCH Project, it cannot be taken as an assessment of the East Pond Expansion.The research nevertheless illustrates a broader consideration for wetland restoration: the presence of water alone does not guarantee that a wetland will sustain a particular ecological community. Water chemistry and the way water reaches a wetland can also affect its ecological conditions. For the SCH Project, maintaining suitable habitat and water conditions will be important to the long-term value of the restored ponds.Flooding the lakebed addresses only part of the problemThe East Pond Expansion is a specific project aimed at improving the habitat in the wetlands, as well as preventing dust from some areas of the exposed lakebed. With 750 acres of area, it is part of a larger project designed to cover more than 9,000 acres in total. The approximately 2,000 acres refer to the combined area of the existing East Pond and its expansion, not to the size of the new expansion alone. However, it should be noted that the ecological issues of the Salton Sea are not limited to the area described above. As a result of reduced inflows and increasing salinity levels, the lake has become smaller and exposed more of the lakebed. The SCH Project is one part of California's broader environmental restoration efforts, and reaching the goal of filling it in 2025 does not mean that all ecological and air-related problems have been solved.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran-backed Houthis claim Saudi airport attack that killed 12 as Middle East tensions rise
articles.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for Saturday's deadly attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which killed 12
articles.body: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for Saturday's deadly attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which killed 12 people and injured more than 300, as a fresh projectile struck the airport complex on Sunday, raising fears of a wider escalation in the Middle East conflict.The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen said Sunday's projectile hit Terminal 4 of the airport, causing a fire. Saudi air defences also intercepted a cruise missile near the airport, although authorities did not immediately provide further details about the latest incident. The airport remained closed following Saturday's attack.The latest developments have intensified concerns that the conflict could spread further, with US President Donald Trump considering whether Washington should join Saudi Arabia's military campaign against the Houthis.Houthis warn airlines to avoid Saudi airportsThe Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi infrastructure amid escalating fighting with forces backed by Riyadh in Yemen. Saturday's strike was the deadliest attack in a Gulf Arab country since the Iran war began, according to reports.The 12 people killed included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Syria and Sudan. More than 300 people were injured, with some reported to be in critical condition.The Houthis have also warned airlines, airport workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, claiming these could be targeted in further attacks.In a statement carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television, the group's foreign ministry warned that further Saudi military action in Yemen would invite retaliation."Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said.The group has exempted airports in Mecca and Medina from its warning. The Saudi-led coalition, meanwhile, has intensified its military campaign and is backing Yemeni government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi advances along the Red Sea coast.Trump weighs US military involvementThe escalation has put Washington under pressure to decide whether to become directly involved in Saudi operations against the Houthis.Trump said on Saturday that the US was considering joining the fight. A direct American intervention could widen the conflict and increase the risk of further attacks on Saudi infrastructure.Saudi Arabia has also faced growing pressure on its air defences as the Houthis continue targeting airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure. The repeated attacks have disrupted aviation and raised concerns about the security of critical infrastructure across the Gulf.The latest violence comes amid a renewed offensive by Yemeni government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, against Houthi positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic waterway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.The narrow passage is an important route for international commercial shipping and energy supplies. Any further disruption could affect global trade and oil prices, particularly as the wider conflict has already placed pressure on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Saudi Arabia faces growing security risksThe airport attack has also struck at a time when Riyadh is hosting a major international energy conference, with other investment-related events planned in the coming days.Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has sought to position the kingdom as a major destination for international business, tourism and investment. Continued attacks on civilian infrastructure could complicate those ambitions.The Houthis' military capabilities have grown in recent years, making the group one of Iran's key regional allies. Although fighting between the rebels and Saudi Arabia had eased following a 2022 ceasefire, tensions have risen again as the conflict in Yemen has intensified and the wider Iran war has spread across the region.Ahmed Nagi, the International Crisis Group's senior analyst for Yemen, warned that the Houthis' strategy could produce the opposite of its intended result.“Rather than pushing Riyadh to step back, attacks on critical Saudi infrastructure could make the Saudis more determined to continue the campaign,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport hit by second Houthi strike in two days
articles.summary: The Yemeni group says it carried out attacks that killed 13 people in Riyadh over the weekend and targeted two airports and oil facilities.
articles.body:
An international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh has been hit by a second strike in as many days, officials have said.

A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile had hit King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, causing a fire in one of its passenger halls. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said there had been injuries.

It comes a day after a strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others, following similar strikes earlier this week.

The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind the attacks and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace.

The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones in the past 24 hours.

They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said.

He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis have said they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, as well as an air strike on the airport in Sanaa.

On Sunday Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition, said air defences had intercepted a missile near the airport in Riyadh, while authorities were dealing with the fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit Passenger Hall No 4.

US President Donald Trump has said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis, while UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh airport attack another dangerous moment in already tense conflict

Saturday's strike was the deadliest single attack on a Gulf Arab country since the war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February. The Saudi-led coalition vowed to respond, calling it a "war crime".

Four Saudi nationals, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt were among the dead, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday that an Indian man had succumbed to the injuries he sustained in the attack.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks and confirmed that a US citizen was killed in the strikes. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he was "appalled".

The UK Foreign Office is advising against all travel to parts of Saudi Arabia, including areas within 10km (6.2 miles) of the border with Yemen, while other western embassies have warned their nationals about travel in the region.

Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said "the Saudi enemy" had launched an air strike on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen's capital. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attack and the BBC has been unable to verify this claim.

Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, vice-president of Yemen's internationally recognised government, called for "decisive actions" from regional and international partners.

Riyadh's airport was struck on Thursday, an attack that killed three Saudi nationals . The Houthis claimed responsibility and said they had used cruise missiles to target the airport.

There were two other deadly attacks on Saudi airports in Abha and Riyadh in the two days prior to that.

The latest uptick in violence comes after a temporary ceasefire between the Houthis and Saudi-led forces, brokered in 2022, collapsed in July.

The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive, prompting Saudi strikes. Yemeni pro-government forces later said they had secured the regions.

The Houthis currently control around a quarter of Yemeni territory and as much as 80% of the country's population. The Iran-backed armed group hopes to eventually seize complete control.

Saudi Arabia fears this would lead to the establishment of an Iranian satellite state on its southern border.

articles.title: Pregnant Woman Was Days Away from Giving Birth When She Was Among 9 Killed in Pennsylvania Shooting
articles.summary: Investigators believe that the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound in the incident, which occurred at a home in Erie on Oct. 9
articles.body:
Angelina Stone was among the nine people killed in a mass shooting in Pennsylvania on Friday, Oct. 9

A family friend said that Stone was just days from giving birth

Investigators believe that the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound in the incident, during which two children also died

A pregnant woman was among the nine people killed in a mass shooting in Pennsylvania.

Angelina Stone and her loved ones were identified as victims of the shooting that occurred at a home in Erie, Pa. around 5 p.m. local time on Friday, Oct. 9, according to CBS News .

The news outlet reported that Stone was just four days from giving birth. The victims also included her two children, brothers and a friend.

Family friend Lisa Simmers told CBS News, "Her two babies were on the spectrum. Innocent children, couldn't have told on that man if they wanted to, and he still killed them."

She added, "It's mind-blowing to me to understand what was happening in that house while we were standing outside. The feeling of helplessness and knowing we couldn't do anything and she was right there."

Simmers told Erie News Now that Stone had a "beautiful" family.

"She was pregnant, about to have her baby in a couple of days. She had a daughter that was almost two, and her son Isiah, who I believe was like four or five, and they were all just beautiful. Beautiful children. And definitely did not deserve what happened to them," the friend said.

A GoFundMe has been created to raise funds for Stone and her children's funeral arrangements. The fundraiser identifies Stone's children as son Isiah, daughter Amari'anna and unborn baby Kyrie. "We have no finances ready to cover this loss, and we have only two weeks from today to get everything done. The funds from this fundraiser will go toward funeral expenses and the fees related to their final arrangements so they can be sent off correctly. This is more than our family can carry alone right now, and we truly need the community to rally around us," the description for the fundrasier reads.

PEOPLE reached out to the Erie County Sheriff's Office on Sunday, Oct. 11, but did not immediately hear back.

A press release on Saturday, Oct. 10 stated that police arrived on the scene within minutes of receiving the alert.

The nine deaths occurred before officers arrived, according to the investigation. There were no additional gunshots after police arrived.

"Our hearts remain with the victims, their loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss of life," the City of Erie said in the release.

Want to keep up with the latest crime coverage? Sign up for PEOPLE's free True Crime newsletter for breaking crime news, ongoing trial coverage and details of intriguing unsolved cases.

Chief of Police Richard Lorah later said in a press conference that police found two deceased females outside the residence within minutes of arriving.

"Video evidence reviewed by investigators shows those two women arriving at the residence, hearing distress, seeking assistance from neighbors and pounding on the door. The audio video also appears to capture muffled gunfire from inside the residence before the suspect emerged and fatally shot both women," he said.

Based on evidence so far, investigators believe that the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The nine dead individuals included eight family members and one family friend.

Lorah also stated that one of the victims was "eight months pregnant."

Victims included a 51-year-old female and a 37-year-old female found outside the residence; a 5-year-old boy and a 1-year-old girl were found on the first floor, and a 24-year-old female, a 44-year-old female, a 19-year-old male and a 21-year-old male on the second floor and stairwell.

The suspected shooter, a 45-year-old, was found dead on the second floor with a firearm.

"Some scenes some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said.

articles.title: A Real Housewives of Toronto star bought a £5.5 million English castle and spent £15 million restoring it; now her plan for a 200-space car park has been rejected
articles.summary: An ancient castle overlooking the Kent countryside has become the centre of a dispute over how a historic property should operate alongside the village
articles.body: An ancient castle overlooking the Kent countryside has become the centre of a dispute over how a historic property should operate alongside the village around it. Dr Ann Kaplan Mulholland, known for appearing on The Real Housewives of Toronto, bought Lympne Castle for £5.5 million and moved to England from Canada in 2023. As reported by The Sun, since then, the Grade I-listed building has undergone an extensive restoration, with reported spending reaching £15 million. The property is also used for weddings and other events, bringing visitors to the rural setting. But a proposal to create a 200-space car park on nearby open land has now been refused, following objections from residents and concerns raised by planning officers.Lympne Castle’s medieval history and its £15 million restorationLympne Castle stands in the village of Lympne in Kent, with views across the surrounding countryside towards the French coast near Calais. Its origins date to the 1080s, making it a building with a history extending well beyond the period of its current owner's television career.The castle served as a residence for the Archdeacon of Canterbury until 1860. Its Grade I listing reflects its historic and architectural significance, placing it among England's most important protected buildings. The designation also means that changes affecting the property and its setting require careful consideration.Kaplan Mulholland, 65, acquired the castle for £5.5 million before relocating from Canada in 2023. She and her husband, plastic surgeon Stephen Mulholland, have invested heavily in the property, with the reported restoration bill reaching £15 million. The couple's wider property portfolio is also substantial, with the Sun reporting that they own 11 properties around the world.Why the proposed 200-space car park was refusedThe latest planning dispute centred on a field near the village hall that Kaplan Mulholland wanted to convert into parking for visitors attending events at the castle. The proposed 200-space facility was intended to accommodate people coming to the property for weddings and other gatherings.Seventeen local residents objected to the application. Among their concerns was the prospect of the parking area becoming an intrusive presence in the village, with fears about noise and the character of the site. The proposal would have involved changing open land that currently contributes to the area's rural appearance.Folkestone and Hythe District Council's planning officers concluded that the scheme would introduce an inappropriate development into the landscape. They described the proposed car park as a visually intrusive and urbanising feature, warning that it would damage the rural character of the area and harm the significance of Lympne Castle.The council also raised concerns about the effect on people living nearby. In its assessment, the proposed use would create unacceptable noise and disturbance, affecting the residential amenity of neighbouring homes.There was a further issue with the application. Planning officers said it had failed to demonstrate compliance with the statutory Biodiversity Net Gain requirements, which are intended to ensure that qualifying developments leave the natural environment in a better state than before. The application therefore did not establish that the proposal would deliver the required biodiversity benefits.The refusal notice stated that the development would erode the rural character of the site and cause harm to the appearance of the surrounding countryside. The decision leaves the proposed 200-space car park off the table, although it does not prevent the owners from considering other parking arrangements.Why Lympne Castle’s parking plans hit a planning obstacleLympne Castle is not simply a private residence. It also operates as a venue for weddings and other events, bringing guests to the property and creating a practical need to manage vehicles arriving at different times.The proposed car park was intended to serve this activity. However, the planning decision illustrates the difficulties that can arise when the requirements of a commercial venue meet the constraints of a protected historic site in a rural village.In conversation with KentOnline, a spokesperson for Lympne Castle said, “We will also continue to make our existing car park available to local people free of charge, and we are grateful to the many residents and visitors who have shown their understanding and support.” The refusal does not mean the venue must stop hosting events. Instead, the owners will need to work within the parking arrangements already available or explore alternatives that can meet planning requirements.Earlier complaints over noise at Lympne CastleThe car park application followed earlier friction between the castle and some nearby residents. In August 2024, Kaplan Mulholland reopened the property's bistro under the name The Naughty Dog. A diesel generator installed behind a stone wall subsequently became a source of complaints about noise.Ian Brown, an 82-year-old neighbour quoted by the Sun, said the sound was sufficiently persistent that he had to keep his windows closed. He described the noise as a constant droning that disturbed the previously peaceful atmosphere of his garden.A castle spokesperson said the generator would be replaced by a new electrical substation. The dispute over the equipment added to the tensions surrounding the property's operation, although the planning refusal for the car park was based on the proposed development's effects on the countryside, neighbouring homes and biodiversity.For residents, the latest decision means that the field will not be turned into the large parking area proposed in the application. For the castle's owners, it leaves the task of accommodating event visitors without making changes that the council considers harmful to the surrounding landscape.A restoration project with a wider public profileKaplan Mulholland and her husband have also invited a film crew to document the castle's renovation. The project has brought additional attention to the couple's move from Canada and their efforts to restore a historic English property on a substantial scale.The restoration of a Grade I-listed building involves more than updating a home to suit its owners. Its historic fabric and architectural features are protected, and work must account for the significance of the building. The reported £15 million investment gives an indication of the scale of the couple's undertaking, though the figure alone does not establish how the spending has been divided between different parts of the project.The castle occupies a reported 139 acres, making it a sizeable estate within the Kent countryside. Its history, views and protected status are part of its appeal, while its use as an event venue creates demands that a purely residential property would not face to the same extent.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bloodied passengers, panic and screams: Survivors recall Riyadh airport strike
articles.summary: Passengers and travellers caught up in a deadly missile strike at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport have recounted scenes of panic, bloodshed and
articles.body: Passengers and travellers caught up in a deadly missile strike at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport have recounted scenes of panic, bloodshed and confusion, as attacks blamed on Iran-backed Houthi rebels intensified across Saudi Arabia. Survivors described hearing a deafening explosion, seeing severely injured people and scrambling to safety as airport sirens sounded.The attack on Saturday killed 12 people and wounded around 300 others, some critically. The airport remained closed on Sunday after another projectile struck a passenger terminal, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen.'My blood ran cold'A 32-year-old Riyadh resident told that a loud explosion shook the airport before alarm sirens triggered panic among passengers, news agency AFP reported."I heard a very loud noise, so loud that I felt the airport shake," he said, "The airport alarm sirens went off, and that's when the panic started."The man said people from Terminal 3 began running towards them, with several visibly covered in blood. Some had suffered severe injuries, including the loss of a hand or an arm."People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us. Some had blood covering their faces," he recounted, "Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood."The scenes left him terrified and unsure how to respond. "My blood ran cold. I didn't know where to go or what to do," he said.Security personnel escorted him and other passengers to a lower floor. They waited there for about an hour before being allowed to leave the scene.As per the report, the passengers spoke on condition of anonymity because of the harsh measures Saudi authorities have threatened against people who speak publicly about strikes.Doctors describe severe injuries, traumaThe impact of the attack was also felt across Riyadh's hospitals, where the health ministry activated emergency protocols to handle a mass-casualty incident. Doctors were ordered to report to medical facilities across the capital.One doctor told that the number of casualties was unlike anything he had witnessed before. Some religious pilgrims travelling to Mecca arrived at hospitals with their white shrouds stained with blood."The numbers were far higher than anything I had ever seen here before," the doctor said. He described patients with severe limb injuries and shards of glass embedded in their faces and eyes."Patients had severe limb injuries and shards of glass embedded in their faces and eyes," he added, "At least four people suffered severe nervous breakdowns."A Saudi military spokesman described the attack as a "full-fledged war crime".'Talk to us': Residents seek answersBeyond the immediate casualties, repeated attacks and limited information from authorities have fuelled anxiety among residents. Saudi Arabia has remained largely silent about the scale and extent of Houthi attacks over the past three months, leaving people uncertain about the risks ahead.Warning text messages that previously alerted residents to incoming barrages have also fallen silent in recent weeks.According to the report by AFP, one frustrated Riyadh resident the lack of communication was adding to the fear."I want to leave from here," the resident said, "I understand they do not want to cause panic but talk to us. Communication channels will make us feel comfortable."Indian family stranded after flight diversionThe attacks have also disrupted air travel, leaving passengers stranded.An Indian national whose transit flight to Riyadh was diverted to Dammam said he, his wife and their young child had to spend the night at the airport. The family said their airline provided no information and their luggage was lost."We spent the night at the airport -- on the floor and chairs," he said, "Not just us, there were at least one dozen other people around me from the same flight who kept waiting through the night."The experience left him unwilling to transit through the kingdom again."I am never flying through Saudi Arabia again," he said.Another traveller, a 39-year-old woman, said she was aboard a plane heading to Riyadh when it suddenly turned back towards Jeddah. The unexpected change left passengers frightened."We panicked," she said.Asked whether she would fly within Saudi Arabia again while the war continued, she ruled out the possibility."Never. I will never live this horror again," she said.Houthi attacks widens Middle East conflictThe Houthis claimed responsibility for the Saturday strike on Riyadh airport, as well as other strikes on Saudi targets. The Saudi-led coalition said another projectile struck a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport on Sunday. There were no immediate details about casualties from the latest strike.The rebels also claimed attacks on King Fahd Airport in Dammam and oil and gas facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia. They warned airlines, airport workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, saying these had become vulnerable to attack. Airports in Mecca and Medina were exempted from the warning.The two sides have been fighting since 2015, when Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in support of the internationally recognised government.The conflict has now raised concerns about the security of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route at the southern end of the Red Sea. articles.title: 'Next PM Vijay 2029’: Placards trigger brief stir at PM Modi event in Chennai
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A brief stir broke out at an official government function attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday after some people
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A brief stir broke out at an official government function attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday after some people displayed placards projecting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the “next PM”.The incident took place at the IIT Madras campus, where PM Modi was addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stone for projects worth around Rs 13,000 crore across Tamil Nadu.CM Vijay was also present at the event.During his speech, P Modi mentioned Vijay's name, prompting a group of people, apparently supporters of the chief minister, to whistle and display handwritten placards bearing Vijay's photographs and slogans, including “Next PM Vijay 2029”, according to news agency PTI.Police personnel deployed at the venue intervened and instructed the individuals to sit down and lower their placards.Although they complied initially, they continued displaying the placards after the police turned away, gesturing towards video cameras.PM Modi and Vijay share stage at Chennai Metro inaugurationThe incident occurred during PM Modi's first visit to Tamil Nadu since the April Assembly elections, which brought Vijay's TVK to power.The prime minister and the chief minister shared the stage during the inauguration of several infrastructure projects. They also jointly flagged off a new Chennai Metro service and travelled on the train.PM Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around Rs 4,900 crore. The new stretch covers approximately 15 km and has 11 elevated stations.The two leaders also jointly inaugurated other scheduled projects during the visit. Vijay received PM Modi on his arrival in Chennai and saw him off before his departure for Delhi.PM Modi vows to work with Vijay for Tamil Nadu's developmentIn his address, PM Modi said his commitment to Tamil Nadu's development would remain unchanged despite changes in government."Governments may change, but my resolve for Tamil Nadu's development, serving its people remains steadfast. With this determination to serve people, together with CM Vijay, we are taking forward the development of the state," he said.PM Modi also highlighted cooperative federalism, saying that the country's development depended on the progress of its states. He recalled his experience of working with several Tamil Nadu chief ministers during his political career.Vijay, meanwhile, said cooperation between the Union and state governments was essential to ensure that people benefited from development initiatives."When the union and state governments work together, its benefit should directly reflect in the lives of the people, and that is our approach," he said.The chief minister also sought the release of Rs 5,110 crore in outstanding central funds under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan scheme without conditions. He called for steps to make Tamil the principal language of the Madras High Court.Vijay also urged the Centre to approve Phase III of the Chennai Metro project, reconsider metro proposals for Coimbatore and Madurai, and consider an inter-state metro line linking Hosur in Tamil Nadu with Bommasandra near Bengaluru. He further sought high-speed rail corridors between Chennai and Kanyakumari and Chennai and Coimbatore.PM Modi praises Tamil language and cultureDuring the visit, PM Modi praised Tamil language and culture and referred to the ancient Tamil classic Thirukkural, describing it as a guide for life.He recalled gifting a Russian edition of the work to Russian President Vladimir Putin and cited its teachings on learning and putting knowledge into practice.PM Modi also paid tribute to national poet Mahakavi Bharati and referred to the continuing relevance of the poet's verse Achamillai, meaning “there is no fear”.The prime minister also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for highway projects, Amrit railway stations, port-related initiatives and the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited refinery in Manali.The visit included meetings and joint public appearances between PM Modi and Vijay as the two governments highlighted their cooperation on infrastructure and Tamil Nadu's development.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on Sunday that Washington’s response to Tehran’s seven conditions for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz was “insufficient”, Iranian state media reported.Rezaei said the United States had accepted some of Iran’s conditions, while others remained unclear. He added that Washington needed to clarify the outstanding issues.Iran had proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming negotiations on its nuclear programme within seven days, provided the United States lifted its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waived sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observed a ceasefire that would also cover Lebanon.Earlier, Iranian foreign minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would respond to a US peace proposal for the West Asia conflict “within the next few days”, amid reports that Washington was preparing military options for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran.Speaking after attending an event, Araghchi said negotiations between Tehran and Washington were continuing, with messages being exchanged through mediators.“The negotiation process is still ongoing, and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, according to Iranian state broadcaster Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB).He added that Tehran had presented its proposal, known as the “Seven-Day Plan”, last month and had received Washington’s views on it.“We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title "Seven-Day Plan," and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gold rush turns deadly: Airstrike kills 13 miners in Sudan-Egypt border zone
articles.summary: At least 13 artisanal gold miners were killed and 28 others injured in an airstrike in the border area between Sudan, Egypt and Libya on Saturday, the
articles.body: At least 13 artisanal gold miners were killed and 28 others injured in an airstrike in the border area between Sudan, Egypt and Libya on Saturday, the Sudan Doctors Network said on Sunday. The identity of those behind the strike remains unclear.The strike hit a gold mine in the mountainous Border Triangle Area, where artisanal and small-scale gold mining is widespread. The medical group warned that the death toll could rise as several injured miners are in serious condition and access to healthcare facilities is limited.Abdel-Aziz Yousef, a survivor, told The Associated Press that an unidentified aircraft struck the mine on Saturday morning. Many people were killed or wounded, while others fled the area fearing further attacks.The Sudan Doctors Network said the miners had repeatedly been warned by Egyptian authorities to evacuate the area, which is reportedly part of Egypt.Gold mining and smuggling fuel Sudan's warGold has played a major role in Sudan's ongoing conflict, with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) accused of smuggling large quantities of the precious metal from the Darfur and Kordofan regions to finance their operations.More than 50% of the gold mined in Sudan was smuggled out of the country, according to a 2024 report by a United Nations Panel of Experts.The border region has also been the focus of Egyptian security operations against illegal mining and smuggling. In June, Egyptian security forces detained hundreds of people, including foreign nationals, along the border with Sudan over alleged involvement in illegal gold mining and smuggling.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dolly Parton's niece wants to learn Welsh after singing with Bronwen Lewis
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's niece, Jada Star, from Tennessee who began learning Welsh during a visit to Wales.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton's niece wants to learn Welsh after recording a Welsh language version of one of her late aunt's most famous songs, Jolene.

Jada Star, a country singer from Tennessee, said: "I truly believe anyone can speak Welsh; it's such a lovely feeling to speak the language, it's a comfortable language."

The track was recorded before Parton's death on 25 August and features vocals from the legendary singer-songwriter herself, who sings alongside Star and singer Bronwen Lewis, from Blaendeulais.

Since the songs release, Star has said she would like to "roam every inch of Wales" and perhaps visit the Eisteddfod one day, as she enjoys learning more about Wales and the Welsh language.

With Star having started learning Welsh on Duolingo, she said that some of her favourite Welsh words so far are Draig (dragon) and Pilipala (butterfly).

"When I came to Wales to see Bronwen, I put a lot of effort into learning Welsh; I was on Duolingo all the time, though I need to pick it up again.

"The app puts sentences together in such a beautiful way, and they're full of dragons," she laughed. "It's fun."

Star explained that the first Welsh words she learned were shwmae and diolch, meaning hello and thank you, to allow her to "greet people in Welsh".

Lewis and Star became friends after she saw a video on TikTok of Lewis singing the song in Welsh.

After travelling to meet Lewis during Pride Cymru, she visited several places. She went from Cardiff to Caernarfon and Conwy, learning Welsh along the way.

Lewis said she was inspired by Star's attitude towards the language: "I never wanted to push singing in Welsh on Jada; the fact that she wanted to and was interested was heartening, she was full of questions about phonetics and pronunciation.

"Jada's attitude towards the language is so healthy; there are many Welsh artists who don't even release Welsh music, so the fact that Jada has done so is amazing."

The pair are currently receiving congratulations from both sides of the Atlantic after releasing their version of Jolene.

"I'm so proud of the track," said Star. "I've been emotional all day and have received messages from Wales that mean the world to me, too.

"I think people really like it; it's something they haven't heard before."

articles.title: CJP says protest will continue till CEC resigns, raises phone hacking doubts
articles.summary: CJP vows protests until CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns; alleges unlawful detentions, assaults and possible phone hacking after seizures, and says Dipke will protest again.
articles.body: New Delhi: Cockroach Janata Party’s Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das at a news conference Sunday raised several questions and doubts regarding the action taken against them as well as thousands of protesters who came out to march on the outfit’s call.In a long interaction with journalists at the Press Club of India, along with CJP member Ratna Singh, SFI member Aishe Ghosh and other Left-backed student activists, Das spoke about the fear that their phones may have been hacked into after being seized. “We told the police they could take our phones, but they must provide a seizure memo and follow the law,” he said. "We were not even allowed to speak to our lawyers. Our phones were kept (from us) for more than 24 hours. We fear they may have been hacked or cloned (our phones), and that documents or evidence may have been planted against us, as has happened with other activists,” he said.The duo said the movement would continue till chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. “Our protests will continue until accountability is fixed, not just in Delhi but across India,” Das said. CJP also alleged that “right-wing extremist groups” were attempting to provoke violence and had “misbehaved with women in Connaught Place.”Ranka said CJP members had attempted another march towards Jantar Mantar Sunday but were detained and assaulted. Members of Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and All India Students’ Federation (AISF) faced similar treatment at the hands of the cops, Ranka added.Das asked why the authorities were going to such lengths to protect Kumar. “What information does Kumar have about govt or its leadership?” he asked.Ranka who, along with Das, is one of the co-conveners of CJP, called the CJP trio’s police detention a “kidnap”. The three were plucked out of a flight Saturday morning when they landed in Delhi. They were released Sunday morning.CJP also alleged that student leaders and protesters were being detained and beaten up. “If they think this will break our spirit, they are mistaken,” they said.The outfit alleged that Dipke, whose grandmother died Saturday during his detention, was denied contact with his family.Das also brought an allegation of custodial torture of protesters and questioned the lack of intervention by National Human Rights Commission. Criticising the restrictions on reporters that police had laid down, he said: “This is an Emergency-like situation for journalism.” He said the more than 40,000 security personnel at Jantar Mantar had made the place a fortress, inconveniencing residents.He also wondered why govt had not called them for a dialogue.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh alleged: “I was followed, my car was chased, and I was photographed as though I were a criminal.” .Singh said that 30 to 35 police personnel surrounded her and told her that she could do one of two things -- either accompany them to a detention centre or return home and remain there. She said she was held inside a car. “How can a citizen be kept in wrongful confinement like this?” she asked.Viraaj Devang, the national president of AISF, who was also at the news conference, said: “Delhi was turned into a cantonment. Ordinary citizens were effectively placed under house arrest, while many protesters arriving from outside Delhi were detained.”SFI national joint secretary Ghosh also questioned the manner in which protesters and activists were detained. Referring to the detention of Dhruv Rathee, she said: “People who were not in uniform entered Dhruv Rathee’s home and took him away without a warrant. This cannot be called the rule of law.”In a message directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Rathee Sunday warned against suppressing dissent to the point where people no longer fear the consequences of speaking out.Dipke, who was not at the news conference as he had returned to Maharashtra to be with his family, posted on X: “Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully.”He was also asked online if he had signed a bond to discontinue protesting. He wrote, “Haven’t signed any bond that says we won’t protest. We will hit the streets again”.Ranka said Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were to blame for the breach of peace. The restrictions and detentions had damaged India’s image in the world, he said.Shortly after the news conference ended, commotion broke out at Press Club of India as police entered the premises. CJP members attempted to leave through the rear gate. Police, after failing to find them at the news conference venue, rushed towards the rear exit. articles.title: Gujarat’s R&B dept plans roadmap on faster projects, quality
articles.summary: Gujarat R&B dept to draft roadmap with timelines and responsibilities after first Chintan Shibir, focusing on faster projects, safety, quality, bridge monitoring, HR and tech.
articles.body: Gandhinagar: The state roads and buildings (R&B) department will prepare an implementation roadmap with defined responsibilities and timelines to translate suggestions made during its first department-level Chintan Shibir into administrative and operational reforms.Held at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar on Oct 8 and 9, the two-day exercise brought together officials and employees to deliberate on five key areas — faster execution of road projects, road safety, infrastructure quality, bridge monitoring, human resource development and greater use of technology in governance.The department said in a statement on Sunday that suggestions and recommendations emerging from the deliberations would be converted into an implementation roadmap, with specific responsibilities, deadlines and continuous monitoring to ensure that the exercise results in tangible improvements in infrastructure delivery and governance.The statement said that five focus groups examined issues concerning faster implementation, quality, maintenance and safety of road projects, design, construction quality and sustainability of govt buildings, bridge safety, regular inspections and modern monitoring systems, capacity-building and skill development and technology adoption, process improvements and transparency.The exercise covered the department’s civil, electrical and mechanical wings, with an emphasis on linking field-level experience to improvements in policy and work processes.The programme also featured sessions on motivation, ergonomics for engineers and effective social media management by govt departments. articles.title: Tunnel dug for orbital rail gives way for 2nd time in a week, damages homes in Nuh
articles.summary: Second cave-in in six days hits Haryana Orbital Rail Corridor tunnel in Nuh, damaging homes and farmland; GAIL pipeline exposed, no injuries; probe ongoing.
articles.body: Gurgaon: A major cave-in occurred for the second time in six days at an under-construction tunnel of Haryana Orbital Rail Corridor (HORC), damaging homes in Nuh district. The incident, which took place in Patuka village under Sahsola gram panchayat on Saturday night around 9pm, caused more than 500 metres of land to collapse, affecting nearly three to four acres of farmland. A Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) pipeline running from Jamnagar to Loni in Ghaziabad was exposed as the soil gave way, but no leakage was reported. No injuries were reported.The affected stretch is located near the point where the tunnel enters Aravali hills and the possibility of seepage caused by weak rock and soil formations is being examined. The tunnel is being constructed at an estimated cost of around Rs 1,200 crore. Work is underway at 80 locations along the HORC project, with experts tasked with monitoring construction. However, the repeated cave-ins have raised fresh questions about the safety of the work, particularly near Aravali hills.The latest cave-in has heightened fears among villagers, who alleged that the construction company had failed to take adequate precautions despite the first incident on Oct 5. Villagers heard a “loud rumbling sound” while inside their homes and rushed outside to find a large pit forming in the fields. The affected area, which initially measured around 300 metres during the night, expanded to more than 500 metres by Sunday morning.A portion of a govt school building was damaged, two houses were affected and one of them was completely razed. A concrete-roofed road connecting the village to Aravali hills was also blocked, while a major electricity tower tilted. A house under construction, where shuttering work was underway, was completely damaged, though nobody was inside at the time. Following the incident, announcements were made from local mosques asking residents to stay away from the site and keep children at a safe distance. Police personnel were deployed to prevent people from approaching the affected area.A team of around two dozen GAIL officials reached the spot to secure the exposed pipeline. More than two dozen senior railway officials, technical experts and investigators also began examining the site. Railway executive director Narendra Chhibber said the incident was unfortunate and the cause of the cave-in was being investigated. He said construction work beneath the tunnel had been stopped after the previous incident five days earlier, ensuring no workers were present when the latest collapse occurred. The affected stretch is located near the point where the tunnel enters Aravali hills, and the possibility of seepage caused by weak rock and soil formations was being examined. Designers and technical experts have been called in, and the area has been barricaded. Chhibber said the damage to farmland was being assessed and affected landowners would be compensated.Senior police officials were rushed to the site on Saturday night and personnel remained deployed there. Residents have been asked to cooperate with the authorities and stay away from the dangerous zone, with action threatened against those violating safety restrictions. Sub-divisional magistrate Jitendra Garg and deputy commissioner Akhil Pilani also visited the site to review the situation and security arrangements.On Oct 5, a large pit measuring around 20 metres across had developed in a farmer’s field. Residents had complained to the police and district administration, alleging negligence by the construction company. They said the latest incident showed that their concerns had not been addressed. Villagers have warned that they will not allow work to continue unless their land is acquired and they receive adequate compensation. articles.title: HP to honour Asian Games medallists
articles.summary: Himachal Pradesh to honour Asian Games medallists in October, awarding Rs 9.03 crore; kabaddi and cricket gold winners get Rs 1 crore each.
articles.body: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh govt will organise an award ceremony in October to honour sports personalities from the state who won medals at the 20th Asian Games in Japan.A govt spokesperson said Ritu Negi, Pushpa Rana, Jyoti Thakur and Bhawana Thakur, members of the gold medal-winning kabaddi team, will each receive Rs 1 crore as prize money.Sawan Barwal, who won a silver medal in the men’s marathon competition, will receive Rs 2.50 crore, while Seema Kumari, who won a bronze medal in the 10,000-metre run, will receive Rs 1.50 crore.The spokesperson said Renuka Thakur, a member of the gold medal-winning cricket team, will receive Rs 1 crore, while judoka Takhelambam Inungambi will get Rs 3 lakh. The state govt will provide a total of Rs 9.03 crore in prize money to these athletes, the spokesperson added.The spokesperson further said that under the revised rules, cash prizes would be distributed equally among all eligible athletes from Himachal Pradesh who are part of a medal-winning Indian team.In such cases, each athlete may receive an amount equal to the prize money prescribed for an individual medal winner. articles.title: DSGMC files police complaint against Kejriwal, AAP over Bangla Sahib protest
articles.summary: DSGMC files complaint with Delhi Police against Arvind Kejriwal, AAP MLAs and workers over alleged Bangla Sahib protest disruption and misleading videos.
articles.body: New Delhi: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) has lodged a complaint with Delhi Police against AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, party MLAs and workers alleging disruption at Gurdwara Sri Bangla Sahib and the circulation of misleading videos on social media.In its complaint dated Oct 11, addressed to the Commissioner of Police, the committee alleged that AAP workers and supporters entered the gurdwara premises in a coordinated manner, staged a protest and created chaos. It also alleged that political slogans were raised inside, violating the sanctity of the place and hurting the religious sentiments of the Sikh community.DSGMC president, Harmeet Singh Kalka, said that AAP MLAs and functionaries circulated videos and social media posts presenting a distorted version of the incident. He said that Kejriwal publicly supported and amplified this narrative.The committee said the sequence of events raised apprehensions that the disruption and circulation of selective videos could have been part of a coordinated attempt to create controversy, malign the gurdwara management and derive political benefit.Describing Bangla Sahib as one of the country’s most revered Sikh religious institutions, the DSGMC said its premises should not be used for political protests, confrontation or propaganda.The committee has asked Delhi Police to identify the people seen in the videos, establish who organised and directed them to enter the premises, preserve the evidence and take legal action against those found involved.On the issue, Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann had earlier said, “I strongly condemn in the harshest terms the BJP’s police forcibly entering Gurdwara Sri Bangla Sahib in Delhi yesterday... History bears witness that the Guru’s abode always keeps its doors open to provide shelter to the needy.”“If the youth of this country protesting entered, the principle of the Guru’s house is that the sevadars would grant them shelter... BJP’s Delhi police, with their Taliban-like attitude, entered Gurdwara Sahib bare-headed and wearing boots... The Sikh community will never forgive the BJP for this shameful act.”In response, Kalka said, “The conduct of the police personnel is a separate matter, but protesters were allegedly provoked and brought into the gurdwara yesterday.
